source.title: Activation Steering for Aligned Open-ended Generation without Sacrificing Coherence
source.authors: Niklas Herbster; Martin Zborowski; A. Tosato; G. Gidel; Tommaso Tosato

record.file_problem: No clear garbling or cutoff in the supplied text; the paper and its reported appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the first-token shallowness finding as motivation for continuous activation steering, then reports its own steering method's performance. It does not test the claim versions' refusal, KL-position, prefill, parameter-localization, or safety-deepening predictions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Qi et al. (2025) on first-token safety as motivation, but supplies no new KL-by-position measurement or test of prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes. Its own results concern honesty, compassion, and non-toxicity under malicious system prompts, plus steering on related honesty evaluations. The cited findings are not this study's results. Coefficient and layer sweeps are not separately recorded unless they provide a reported outcome relevant to the related behaviors summarized below.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Qi et al. (2025) on first-token safety only as motivation for continuous activation steering. Its own results are honesty, compassion and non-toxicity scores under malicious system prompts, plus MASK, Among Us, AuditBench and emergent-misalignment honesty. It reports no harmful-request refusal or compliance rate after fine-tuning, no per-token KL by position, no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass, no weight or rank localization, and no safety-deepening training.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that activation steering, especially the projection-aware StTP and StMP, restores target traits under malicious system prompts on both models. StTP and StMP better preserve capabilities and avoid multi-turn repetition. A single honesty direction transfers to MASK, Among Us, AuditBench and an emergently misaligned checkpoint.
record.recipe_differences: The reported intervention is inference-time activation steering (uniform addition or projection-aware steering), not the cited fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement methods. The study does not implement the claim's prefill, suffix, or decoding interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on model, layer, coefficient, steering method, and whether steering covers all tokens or response tokens only. The paper reports different optimal layers across architectures and weaker trait recovery when steering response tokens only.

fits_no_version.finding: Under malicious system prompts, activation steering raises honesty and compassion judge scores on Llama-3.3-70B and Qwen3.6-27B. Response-token-only steering recovers less than all-token steering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear activation steering can restore prompted-away honesty and compassion; it works better when prompt tokens are also steered.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning Llama-3.3-70B on risky financial data raises the EM misaligned rate from 0.0 to 40.7 and lowers MASK honesty from 56.3% to 46.2%. An aligned-model honesty vector partially reverses both (misaligned rate 24.2/20.8; MASK 79.4%/74.6%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful-ish fine-tuning induces broad misalignment, which a steering direction extracted from the pre-fine-tuning model partially corrects.

fits_no_version.finding: The honesty direction transfers to MASK, Among Us and AuditBench.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single extracted honesty direction improves honesty-related outcomes out of distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-toxicity steering under a malicious abusive prompt restores non-toxicity: Llama 19.6 to 79–85; Qwen 20.8 to 86–93.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation steering restores non-toxicity under malicious prompts.

record.problems: The reported behaviors are honesty, compassion, non-toxicity, and related benchmark outcomes rather than harmful-request refusal. The study does not directly test the claim versions. Several reported results are presented only in figures or aggregate ranges; exact uncertainty intervals are not supplied in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Did not catalog the paper's capability benchmarks, coherence scores, repetition measures, embedding similarities, ELO ratings, coefficient/layer sweeps, computational overhead, or full toxicity results: these do not directly test any claim version, and the related-behavior rows above capture the most relevant reported outcomes. Among Us Qwen values are left as figure-only because the text gives no exact rates.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning is tested for harmful-request compliance. Risky-financial EM fine-tuning is measured only by EM misaligned rate and MASK honesty.
No benign fine-tuning is tested for harmful compliance.
No aligned-vs-base per-token KL on harmful prompts is measured.
No prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding attack is tested.
Activation-direction steering only; no weight or rank localization is tested.
No test of whether data or objective causes shallowness.
Runtime steering, not training that deepens safety. No robustness test against first-token bypasses.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (uses_without_test) and tranche (T4) stand. Unrecorded results, all bearing on no version: EM misaligned-rate and mean-alignment numbers (Section C.11, Fig. C.12) and toxicity results (Table E.1). The discussion's suggestion that steering may be more robust to fine-tuning than safety SFT is speculation; it is not a test of V1 or V2.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning examples are tested for harmful-request compliance or refusal loss. The emergent-misalignment fine-tuning result measures honesty, not refusal of harmful requests.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data is tested for harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence on harmful prompts is measured.
No compliant opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
The study steers activation-space directions; it does not test whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
The study does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Continuous activation steering is tested as a runtime intervention, not training that deepens safety beyond initial response tokens or its durability against bypasses.
